newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money rates drop on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money rates drop on rate cut.

text.p: The cut in the Central Bank's overnight rates nudged down Manila overnight money to an average of 10.28125 on Tuesday from 10.46875 percent, traders said.
Rates moved in a lower range from 10.3125 to 10.28125 percent, with lenders numbering 28 and borrowers 18.
The Central Bank cut its overnight borrowing and lending rate by 0.1875 percentage point each to 10.25 and 12.75 percent, respectively.
The Central Bank's action was triggered by the sharp fall in Treasury bill rates in the primary auction last Monday with the benchmark 91-day rate now at 10.159 from 10.564 percent.
In the secondary market, quoted rates followed the Central Bank's move.
There were few borrowers for short-term bills. "The rates were too low," a dealer said.
Banks' buying focus, however, was on the long-term issues of two years and above before rates decline further ahead of the auction of the two-year T-bonds later in the day.
Traders said they expected the two-year bonds to fetch a coupon rate from 11.25/11.375 from the previous 11.875 percent.
A Reuter poll of seven financial insitutions showed an offer rate of 10.0 to 10.125 percent on the three-month bills.
